answer.rationale: The line is at 94% with no buffer and the primary contract lapses in 14 days, so a primary switch or a lapse would raise delivery risk and violate the TCO-without-added-risk objective. Incumbent continuity has previously kept integrations and deliveries stable (c1). Renewal-time benchmarking has moved price and terms (c4), and a longer incumbent commitment has cut unit cost without shrinking scope (c6); those levers, plus the already-in-hand low-cost quote, are the path to chase the 18% cut without a migration. Deferral and a second-source-only move would leave the expiring primary unaddressed. Verifying c2 because it is the load-bearing claim that a low-cost primary switch was operationally cheap; if the source record hides delivery or quality caveats, that confirms staying off a switch at zero buffer. Whether the incumbent can actually reach 18% in this window remains unknown.
